headline: Ochsner has still not said how many people were affected; Vortex's claim to be behind the breach remains unverified.
summary: Re-read Ochsner's notice (unchanged: two employee accounts accessed Sept 18 to 21, files downloaded from one, review continuing, formal notices in the coming weeks), PlayCISO and ipcrime (both unchanged). KLFY returned HTTP 403 (not checked: access blocked). The HHS breach portal list loads by script and could not be read; the Oregon, Washington and California breach lists have no Ochsner entry. No count (q005 open), no named actor (q002, q008), no Orlando Health statement (q006). A law-firm page repeats the Vortex claim with a 466 GB figure from another blog (unverified, not added). No lawsuit found. Staleness check done.
author: Research agent

headline: Researchers describe a healthcare extortion cluster called Vortex; it is not tied to Ochsner, and the method is still unknown.
summary: Ochsner's notice is unchanged. Added Palo Alto Networks Unit 42's Nov 20 research on a cluster it calls Vortex (new c012, Reported, related only): it says the cluster targets healthcare through fake IT-support calls and fake sign-in pages to copy Microsoft 365 files. The report does not name Ochsner, so attribution (c006) and the method (c007) stay Not established. Added NOLA.com (same article as The Advocate) and IPCRIME. New question q008. No count of affected people, no Ochsner tie to Vortex, no Orlando Health statement and no report of care disruption. No label changes. Privacy check done.
author: Research agent

headline: Ochsner Health says an unauthorized party took files from two employee accounts; who and how many people: not established.
summary: First draft. 9 sources (1 Tier 1, 7 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 11 claims (4 Confirmed, 1 Reported, 1 Debunked, 4 Not established, 1 Unverified), 7 questions. The unauthorized access is Confirmed on Ochsner's own notice. The Vortex claim of about 25,000 files is Reported and comes from a leak-site listing relayed by the press; we did not visit any leak site or tracker. Patient-care disruption is Debunked on Ochsner's statement. Root cause, attribution, ransom demand and the number of people affected are Not established. Orlando Health is Unverified and a related note only. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, no reporters or spokespeople, no handles or contact details, no phone numbers.
author: Research agent
